# New Zealand Property Market Profile

## Structural Characteristics

- Population: ~5.3M, highly urbanized (Auckland ~1.7M)
- Housing stock: ~2.0M dwellings
- Owner-occupation rate: ~65% (declining from ~74% in 1990s)
- Dominant housing type: Standalone houses (80%+), townhouses/apartments growing
- Key institutions: REINZ (data), RBNZ (macroprudential), MBIE (housing policy), Kāinga Ora (state housing)

## Historical Cycle Phases

| Period | Phase | Real Price Change | Key Driver |
|--------|-------|------------------|------------|
| 1992-1997 | Boom | +40% | Immigration, financial deregulation |
| 1998-2001 | Stabilization | Flat | Asian Financial Crisis, RBNZ tightening |
| 2002-2007 | Boom | +85% | Immigration, credit expansion, tax advantage |
| 2008-2009 | Correction | -10% | GFC, credit crunch |
| 2010-2016 | Boom | +55% | Low rates, housing shortage, Chinese buying |
| 2017-2019 | Stabilization | Flat | LVR restrictions, foreign buyer ban |
| 2020-2021 | Boom | +40% | COVID stimulus, record-low rates, FOMO |
| 2022-2024 | Correction | -15 to -20% | RBNZ aggressive hiking (OCR 0.25% → 5.50%) |
| 2024-2025 | Stabilization/Early Recovery | Flat to +3% | Rate cuts beginning, migration surging |

## Key Macro Drivers (NZ Specific)

### 1. Net Migration
- Dominant short-term housing demand driver
- +50K/year = normal, +100K+ = extreme pressure
- Auckland absorbs ~50% of net migration
- Record inflows (2023-2024) directly reversed early-correction price weakness

### 2. RBNZ OCR
- Mortgage rates in NZ are predominantly 1-2Y fixed → fast passthrough
- OCR 0.25% (2021) → 5.50% (2023) = most aggressive hiking cycle in OECD
- Every 100bp OCR change → ~$150-200/week change in mortgage payments (median Auckland mortgage)
- DSR at 5.50% OCR near record levels (~55% in Auckland)

### 3. Housing Supply
- Chronic undersupply estimated at 40-100K dwellings (varying estimates)
- Auckland Unitary Plan (2016) upzoning increased supply responsiveness
- Construction costs +30% since 2019 (materials + labor)
- Building consent cycle turning down (2023 peak → 30% decline)

### 4. Tax Policy (Unique NZ Features)
- No capital gains tax (except bright-line test: 2 years for existing, 5 years for new builds)
- No stamp duty / land tax
- Interest deductibility: Removed (2021) → Phased back in (2024)
- These features make NZ property tax-advantaged vs. almost all other OECD countries

### 5. Foreign Buyer Ban (2018)
- Non-resident foreign buyers effectively banned (Overseas Investment Act)
- Exceptions: Australians, Singaporeans (FTA), new builds in large developments
- Reduced foreign demand but mostly symbolic — foreign buyers were ~3% pre-ban

## Key Data Sources

| Data | Source | Frequency | Access |
|------|--------|----------|--------|
| HPI (House Price Index) | REINZ | Monthly | Public (headline), paid (detail) |
| Sales Volumes | REINZ | Monthly | Public |
| Days to Sell | REINZ | Monthly | Public |
| Inventory (months) | REINZ | Monthly | Public |
| Auction Clearance Rates | Interest.co.nz | Weekly | Public |
| Rental Price Index | MBIE Tenancy Services | Monthly | Public |
| Building Consents | Stats NZ | Monthly | Public (Aotearoa Data Explorer) |
| Mortgage Lending (by LVR, DTI) | RBNZ (C31, C35) | Monthly | Public |
| Household Debt Service Ratio | RBNZ | Quarterly | Public |
| Housing Credit Growth | RBNZ (C5) | Monthly | Public |

## Affordability Benchmarks (NZ Specific)

| Metric | Auckland | Wellington | Christchurch | National |
|--------|----------|-----------|-------------|----------|
| Median Price | $1.0-1.2M | $750-850K | $650-700K | $800-900K |
| Price-to-Income | ~10-12x | ~7-8x | ~6-7x | ~8-9x |
| Price-to-Rent | ~28-32x | ~22-25x | ~18-20x | ~25-28x |
| Deposit Required (20%) | $200-240K | $150-170K | $130-140K | $160-180K |
| Years to Save Deposit* | 12-15yr | 8-10yr | 6-8yr | 10-12yr |
| Mortgage as % of Income** | 55-60% | 40-45% | 30-35% | 45-50% |

*Assuming 10% savings rate on median household income
**At 6.5% mortgage rate, 25Y term, 20% deposit

## RBNZ Macroprudential Framework

| Tool | Current Setting | Impact |
|------|----------------|--------|
| LVR (Owner-Occupier) | 20% max >80% LVR | Limits high-leverage lending |
| LVR (Investor) | 5% max >70% LVR | Constrains investor leverage |
| DTI (Proposed) | Under consultation | Would cap debt-to-income |
| Debt Serviceability Test | 1% buffer over actual rate | Stressed borrowing assessment |

## Key Risks & Outlook

### Downside Risks
- OCR sustained above 5% → mortgage resets at higher rates (2024-2025 wall)
- Unemployment rising → forced sales increase
- Net migration reversing (Australian wage premium attracting NZ workers)
- Insurance costs rising (climate risk, earthquake premiums)

### Upside Risks
- OCR cuts faster than expected → mortgage rates fall, sentiment improves
- Net migration sustained at high levels → demand pressure
- Supply response insufficient (construction sector capacity constraints)
- Foreign buyer ban relaxation (ACT/NZ First policy)

### Cycle Assessment
- Phase: Stabilization → Early Recovery (2025)
- Correction depth: -15-20% real from peak (moderate by NZ historical standards)
- Rebound risk: High if migration + rate cuts coincide
- Affordability: Still severely stretched — structural, not just cyclical
